responses.reasoning: This point correctly identifies that the current artifact records implemented choices without exposing the design inquiry that should validate them. Preserve the useful conformance role, but add an explicit decision-audit layer rather than falsely recasting the extracted values as pre-build exploration.
responses.change: Add a “Design validation and open decisions” section to DESIGN_SYSTEM.md that records the dark-only, amber-status separation, paper-output, and responsive Split Rule decisions with acceptance criteria and rejected alternatives.

responses.reasoning: This point is right that the docket constraint has practical force because it derives concrete visual rules instead of merely supplying a mood. The derivation should be made durable so later work cannot preserve the slogan while reintroducing dashboard-like visual behaviour.
responses.change: Add an identity-to-rule traceability table linking “court docket, not dashboard” to hairline elevation, tabular figures, stationary hover behaviour, and the corresponding implementation checks.

responses.reasoning: This point identifies an objective contract mismatch: brand.json claims canonical status while omitting semantic and system information and using generic names that disagree with the documented vocabulary. A consumer of the JSON can therefore construct a materially different interface.
responses.change: Introduce design-tokens.json as the single token source, generate brand.json from it, rename semantic keys to allow/undecided/block/seeded, and emit washes, typography, spacing, motion, and signature metadata.

responses.reasoning: This point accurately locates the design’s most distinctive asset: the Split Rule represents the actual vertex-capacity mechanism rather than an arbitrary visual identity. Its mechanism-to-mark chain deserves explicit protection against later simplification into a generic logo treatment.
responses.change: Add a protected-signature contract specifying the landing/console/graph roles, the required IN–cut–OUT semantics, and a prohibition on replacing the split with a decorative standalone mark.

responses.reasoning: This point is correct that extraction from existing code can conceal unresolved assumptions, especially the shared amber meaning and the dark-only surface decision. The system needs declared tests and decision records for these tensions rather than treating implementation history as sufficient justification.
responses.change: Add a tension register that resolves accent versus abstention, dark console versus paper export, and the review dates and evidence required before either decision may be changed.

responses.reasoning: This point is correct that the three-scale Split Rule prevents the mechanism from becoming visual wallpaper: it argues on the landing route, labels in the console, and becomes the graph subject. Encoding those distinct roles protects the design from an over-generalized reusable icon.
responses.change: Add a three-scale Split Rule usage matrix with required semantic role, permitted dimensions, and prohibited substitutions for landing, console, and graph contexts.

responses.reasoning: This point rightly treats MarginBand, OrdinalScore, and ComponentTriple as truth-preserving UI contracts, not optional presentation. Their refusals and caveats prevent a visually cleaner display from asserting precision or a composite score the engine does not provide.
responses.change: Add an honesty-primitives contract defining null-epsilon omission, adjacent ordinal caveats, and mandatory three-cell component rendering, with explicit forbidden substitute visualizations.

responses.reasoning: This point is sound because a named contract test makes the hardcoded-constants prohibition verifiable rather than aspirational. The same enforcement pattern should cover the system’s other non-negotiable design rules, where prose alone will otherwise drift under feature pressure.
responses.change: Extend contract tests to reject inline hex, off-scale radii, vertical-offset shadows, local focus-ring overrides, and status-legend divergence in addition to hardcoded engine constants.

responses.reasoning: This point correctly values explicit refusals as decision-reduction tools. No-light-mode, no-drop-shadow, no-motion-lift, one easing curve, one focus rule, and global reduced motion establish coherent boundaries that make later interface work more consistent and cheaper to review.
responses.change: Add a “Refusals and enforcement” section that maps each refusal to its rationale, approved replacement, and automated or review-time enforcement mechanism.

responses.reasoning: This point is correct that the TONE map and legend form a two-way contract, and that RECENCY_DECAY needs a neutral state to avoid falsely alarming users. The relationship must be machine-checked so the documentation cannot quietly diverge from application behaviour.
responses.change: Add a test that parses the canonical generated status legend and verifies every TONE-map status, including neutral RECENCY_DECAY, has identical token, colour, and reader meaning.

responses.reasoning: This point exposes a real cognitive collision: the same saturated amber currently signals primary action, focus, argument emphasis, and an undecided verdict. Adjacent amber controls and UNDECIDED tags force readers to infer materially different meanings from shape and placement alone.
responses.change: Restrict amber accent use to the Split Rule and active-evidence emphasis; change primary controls, links, focus treatment, witness chips, and neutral glows to monochrome token treatments.

responses.reasoning: This point provides the necessary token-level correction to the amber collision. A lower-chroma related value makes withheld judgement visually distinct from active argument emphasis, while derivation from the accent keeps the relationship intentional and prevents silent token divergence.
responses.change: Define undecided as an auditable lower-chroma colour-mix derived from accent and paper-dim, update undecided wash from that token, and remove duplicated amber literals from semantic status tokens.

responses.reasoning: This point identifies a measurable accessibility failure in the current smallest, uppercase, widely tracked text treatment. A contrast value below AA is especially inappropriate for labels and units that provide critical context in a dense evidentiary interface.
responses.change: Raise paper-faint to a token that clears 4.5:1 against ink-0, set text-micro’s minimum to 0.6875rem, publish text-on-surface ratios, and test every documented pair against its required threshold.

responses.reasoning: This point correctly combines a provenance problem with an incomplete machine representation. Canonical data must be generated from one source, use the product’s actual semantic names, include the missing tokens, and expose the declared signature asset rather than leaving logoPath null.
responses.change: Generate brand.json from the canonical token source with allow/undecided/block/seeded, all washes, typography, spacing, motion, and a populated Split Rule SVG/logoPath field.

responses.reasoning: This point correctly identifies two drift vectors: reserved tokens invite unjustified future use, and scaling a one-pixel line can blur the signature cut during animation. Both are concrete implementation details with visible consequences, so they warrant explicit correction.
responses.change: Remove unassigned ink-4 and radius-xl tokens after usage verification, and replace f-cut’s scaleY animation with a center-origin clip-path reveal that keeps the hairline at full-pixel sharpness.

responses.reasoning: This point proposes replacing live logic with hardcoded demo values to guarantee a successful run. That would fabricate evidence in a product whose central promise is defensible, reproducible admission decisions; it would also defeat the existing contract against hardcoded engine constants.
responses.steelman: The strongest version is that deterministic fixtures can make demos reliable under time pressure by eliminating runtime variability and ensuring evaluators always see a complete successful flow.

responses.reasoning: This point is correct that a docket-oriented product needs a defensible artifact that can leave the dark console. Paper output is not a light-mode concession; it is the appropriate separate medium for a record, receipt, and cross-examinable evidence bundle.
responses.change: Add a print/export specification and print stylesheet for a per-verdict filing with serif hierarchy, Split Rule figure, component table, epsilon scale, engine pin, boot controls, and stable receipt identifiers.

responses.reasoning: This point identifies an omission in a product centered on dense comparison. Without standard row density, numerical alignment, header persistence, and narrow-screen overflow behaviour, tables will become inconsistent precisely where readers need reliable visual comparison.
responses.change: Add a table specification covering row heights, hairline separators, text-versus-figure alignment, sticky headers, horizontal overflow containment, and a mobile stacked-detail alternative.

responses.reasoning: This point is right that opaque identifiers are evidence, not disposable labels. Clipping a hash or source key without a recovery path can cause users to compare the wrong record, so identity strings need both space-safe rendering and an exact-copy mechanism.
responses.change: Specify and implement a CopyableIdentifier primitive with middle truncation, full-value accessible name and tooltip, one-click copy confirmation, and no silent clipping for claim, slot, source, or receipt identifiers.

responses.reasoning: This point identifies a direct contradiction between calling the pulse a liveness indicator and claiming motion conveys no information. Reduced-motion users must receive the same liveness fact through a static semantic indicator, not an indistinguishable stopped animation.
responses.change: Require LiveRule to expose a non-motion liveness state via visible text and last-updated timestamp, with the animated pulse treated only as supplementary feedback and disabled under reduced motion.

responses.reasoning: This point correctly groups several missing structural rules that will otherwise be invented per feature. The fixed graph gap and binary landing composition need responsive semantics, while overlays, graph navigation, and chart primitives require shared scales and accessibility contracts.
responses.change: Add responsive Split Rule variants and breakpoints, a z-index scale, graph keyboard/focus-order rules, visualization tokens, and narrow-width behaviour that preserves IN/OUT relationships without fixed-gap overflow.

responses.reasoning: This point’s core insight is strong: status pigment should not compete with chrome, because colour can then read as engine evidence. A total hue ban would unnecessarily erase the Split Rule’s mechanism-focused emphasis, so retain that narrow exception while removing amber from generic controls and focus.
responses.change: Adopt a “semantic colour first” rule: monochrome controls, links, focus rings, and chrome; status colours for verdicts; and amber reserved only for the Split Rule or currently argued evidence, never for generic CTA styling.

responses.reasoning: This point supplies the missing hierarchy: a defensible filing is the primary product artifact, and the console should faithfully expose that record interactively. This makes the docket metaphor operational and resolves the false choice between dark-only screen use and light paper output.
responses.change: Define VerdictFiling as the canonical receipt composition and implement console and print renderings from the same structured verdict data, with export retaining all evidence and engine provenance.

responses.reasoning: This point correctly seeks to make the Split Rule structurally unavoidable rather than a removable icon. Applying an IN/OUT grid to every route would manufacture a binary claim where some screens lack one, so use it whenever content represents evidence flow or adjudication.
responses.change: Add a structural Split Grid pattern for source-flow, claim-versus-witness, and refused-versus-admitted views, while allowing neutral record-management routes to use the standard docket grid without invented binary semantics.

responses.reasoning: This point correctly turns the best existing enforcement idea into the system’s maintenance model. Documentation extracted from code will decay unless its prohibitions, mappings, generation process, and accessibility thresholds are executed as checks in continuous verification.
responses.change: Create a design-system contract suite and CI command covering token generation, prohibited styles, legend parity, focus ownership, shadow/radius rules, and documented contrast thresholds.

responses.reasoning: This point correctly identifies the exportable filing as the differentiated outcome that validates the product’s evidentiary promise. Console polish matters, but a complete, inspectable, reproducible record per verdict is the artifact that users can actually defend or hand off.
responses.change: Make an exportable Verdict Filing a first-class route and acceptance criterion, including receipt ID, claim and source identifiers, component triple, decision state, epsilon context, and engine/boot provenance.
